messages:
alice: Heads up — the Python async sample app for tool/function calling is blowing up when I pass a Pydantic model as the structured output. Repro is tiny and consistent.
alice: Repro steps: install redwood-sdk==0.10.1, pydantic==2.2.1, run the async sample with response_model=MySchema and it errors on deserialize.
alice: Example call I used:
```python
from redwood.async_client import AsyncClient
from myapp.schemas import MySchema

client = AsyncClient(api_key=os.getenv('REDWOOD_API_KEY'))
resp = await client.tools.call('extract_entities', input_text, response_model=MySchema)
# expecting MySchema instance but get exception
```

ben: Can you paste the stack trace? :eyes:

alice: Stack (truncated):
```
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "app.py", line 42, in <module>
    resp = await client.tools.call(...)
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.11/site-packages/redwood/sdk/tools.py", line 128, in call
    return await self._handle_response(response, response_model)
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.11/site-packages/redwood/sdk/tools.py", line 210, in _handle_response
    return response_model.parse_obj(parsed)
AttributeError: 'type' object has no attribute 'parse_obj'
```

alice: Looks like the SDK is assuming pydantic v1 API (parse_obj) even when using v2 models.
carla: Which Python and pydantic versions? Also which example did you start from (link to sample app)?
alice: Python 3.11.4, pydantic 2.2.1, sample app from docs: https://repo.internal/redwood/python-samples/toolcall-async.md (local copy).

ben: Huh — we changed ToolResult typing last week to be generics + avoid importing pydantic directly. Prob regressed the v2 path in the async helper.
dave: Quick workaround: pass response_model=None and postprocess with pydantic BaseModel(**resp) or use `return_raw=True` if available. Example:
```python
raw = await client.tools.call('extract_entities', input_text, return_raw=True)
obj = MySchema.model_validate(raw)  # pydantic v2 method
```

alice: Confirmed — workaround works. Using model_validate on v2 works fine. Thanks.
erin: Sorry for the friction. @alice can you open a minimal repro (small repo or gist) and drop the link here? I'll take ownership and add a unit test for async tool path + pydantic v2. Also include your env/lockfile.
alice: Yep — created a tiny gist with steps and failing test: https://gist.github.com/alice/abcdef12345 — includes Dockerfile and tox matrix.

ci-bot: CI / python-toolcall-tests failed for commit 0b3f9e — see https://ci.internal/redwood/1234 :robot_face:

ben: Thanks — erin, assigning to you. I'll put a label `sdk-bug:toolcall-pydantic` on the issue.

carla: Can we also update the sample docs to show the pydantic v2 pattern as explicit workaround until fixed? Newcomers keep hitting this.
erin: Good call. I'll do a docs patch in the same PR (examples + changelog). Planning to push a fix and a test by EOD tomorrow.

alice: Awesome, thanks all. Leaving the workaround in my app for now. :+1:

ben: :thumbsup:

alice: :facepalm: — bumped into this during onboarding for a new hire, so putting it here to save others.
